rationale: Both candidates independently converge on the same core real issues (SoulX Singer now silently gets Cache-DiT enabled untested, other _dit_modules consumers like diffusion_model_runner.py still use plain getattr on dotted paths, test assertions don't pin the actual regression, and the fix duplicates module_collector.py's existing attrgetter resolver), which is strong evidence both are well-grounded rather than fabricated. Y goes deeper on each: it traces the actual regression history via git archaeology, ran the test suite locally (132 passed) and checked CI, gives a mechanistic (if unverifiable) explanation for why SoulX's CFG branches would break DBCache, and adds a sharper critique of the is_cached guard's real effect plus concrete suggested code/log lines. X's sweep-style report is noisier (many routine confirmations diluting the few substantive findings) but its dedicated inline findings are comparably specific and well-evidenced. Neither has a LATENT GAP CHECK section so gap_hit is false for both; recall is roughly comparable on this thin ground truth (mainly the module_collector.py dedup suggestion), with Y's presentation and follow-up scope giving it a slight edge in actionability and precision.
